newsitem.title: RUSSIA: MinFins skyrocket on Eurobond, debt news.
newsitem.headline: MinFins skyrocket on Eurobond, debt news.

text.p: Russian MinFins skyrocketed on Monday, with some tranches hitting records on news Russia's new Eurobond would be issued in March and the London Club rescheduling closed in spring, dealers said.

"All day long, prices have been growing constantly and steadily," Moscow Business World Bank chief dealer Sergei Kovzharov said. "We have not seen such a stable rise since Russia got a (credit) rating in October."
He said tranches three and four hit all-time highs.

Russia will launch a one billion mark ($609.3 million) Eurobond to be led by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and CS First Boston in early March and will issue a total of about $3 billion in Eurobonds this year, Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Monday.
He also said the rescheduling of Russia's London Club debt would close at the end of March or early in April.
"Such a flow of positive news supported by comments from (French President Jaques) Chirac about (President Boris) Yeltsin's health is always positive for the market," Kovzharov said.
Chirac met Yeltsin on Sunday to discuss NATO expansion.
An International Moscow Bank dealer said buying in the fourth tranche started on Friday after news JP Morgan planned to issue a 100 million mark bond secured by the MinFin fourth tranche.

Dealers said it was difficult to forecast what would happen in the next few days as investors were waiting to see whether the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee decides to raise interest rates at its meeting on February 4-5.
